THE OPEN SEA ROUND THE RIG, and exactly one tile type on this map carries it: deep water. Everything a player
walks on out here is deck plate, planking or three-thousand-year-old stone, and none of it declares an
encounter, so the platform itself is silent -- which is right, because a working industrial site is a place
the wildlife has already left.

THE TABLE IS OPTIONAL CONTENT TWICE OVER. It can only fire for a player who has Swim (granted below, in the
lower temple) and who has chosen to go over the side, and the only thing out there is the drowned colonnade at
4-6,28-29 with a Deep Vessel on it. Rate 90 rather than a route's 150 accordingly: nobody should be dragged
through four fights to cross forty tiles of open water for one item.

MEASURED against the level tests/helpers/simulate.mjs puts the player at leaving Crownspire -- 45 raising a
team, 60 solo. One kin, novice play, no items, mean band then worst-of-band, sprigling / cinderpaw / rilltail:
   L44  100/58/95  worst 99/50/92      L46  100/70/97  worst 100/61/95
The Flame column is the one that matters and it is the reason these levels are 36-39 rather than the low
forties they started at. Tide is double into Flame and Flame is half into Tide, so an ocean is to a Cinderpaw
player what Embercoil was to a Bramblehusk one; at the levels this table was first cut to, the same column read
FORTY-THREE percent. Dropping the band two levels bought fifteen points in the weakest column and cost nothing
anywhere else, and this is water nobody is required to enter.

Nothing is above its own evolution level -- Currentail evolves at 20, Tidewrack at 29, Clatterclaw at 27, and
Gullswift, Anchorling, Brinewisp and Bladderwrack do not evolve at all. Weights total 100.
